[[Category:Proper name]]
The '''Hubble radius ($R_H$)''' denotes the scale around which [[classical mechanics]] ceases to be valid.

At any given instance in time,
$$
R_H=cH^{-1}
$$

where $H$ is the [[Hubble parameter]] at that time.

== Significance ==

Relativistic effects become relevant when relative speed between objects $|v| \to c$.

At $R_H$, by [[Hubble-Lemaître law]],

$$
v=HR_H=c.
$$

Therefore, at scale near the Hubble radius, even stationary objects can no longer be modelled with [[classical mechanics]] because of [[cosmic expansion]].
